title.narrative: YOUNG WOMEN FOR AWARENESS, AGENCY, ADVOCACY, AND ACCOUNTABILITY (YW4A) PROGRAMME

description.narrative: The programme aims to strengthen and diversify young women’s participation and amplify their voices to effectively influence decision-making towards gender-just laws, policies, norms, and practices related to their bodily integrity and equal participation.The programme will achieve this through 4 main outcomes: 1.Strengthening the advocacy capacity of 27 women’s rights organizations (WROs) to amplify young women’s voices in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025. 2.Enhancing the leadership of 17,540 young women to effectively engage in collective action and decision-making in public, private, and civic spaces in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025. 3.Transforming social norms and practices of 22 faith-based organizations (FBOs) that constrain young women’s rights in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025. 4.Influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilisation and implementation of 18 laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya and South Sudan by 2025.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.2 (WRG049y) “IO2 Strengthened individual leadership of 13,700 young women across the four countries".

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices. Leadership roles are measured by capacity to apply different forms of leadership training (to peers), willingness to become role models, self-confidence and efficacy, planning and facilitation skills, public speaking, advocacy, willingness to engage in policy change and with actors in public and civic decision-making spaces, exercise of leadership roles in the community, women’s groups, CSOs and political spaces, mobilization of young women, networking.

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices.

comment.narrative: Before the RiseUp! Training of Trainers started, 22 Cohort 1 young women took part in the Young Women Leadership (YWL) assessment as to measure their leadership capacity. The YWL score presents the young women's current capacity following the three classifications: Experienced, Aspiring, and Starting. In Egypt, the majority of Cohort 1 participants fell under the category of "Aspiring" in terms of young women's leadership, indicating that they perceived themselves to be in the middle of their leadership journey. A smaller percentage of respondents were classified as "Experienced" leaders, indicating that they already considered themselves leaders but may need further development. One respondent, who was also a self-identified marginalised young woman, classified as being in the "Starting" phase of her leadership journey. The trends observed among marginalized young women were similar to those of the larger sample, with a majority aspiring to become leaders and fewer having experienced leadership.

The Cohort 1 training target for 2021 was set at 24 young women. Apart from training the young women, the objectives were also to translate and localize the Rise Up! Training materials to the Egyptian context.
I believe this already includes a narrative explanation.

The total endline target for Egypt has not changed following the MTR, and is set at 4,200 young women. During 2023 Egyptian partners have trained substantially more young women than anticipated. To achieve the endline target in Egypt, at least 2,027 young women should be trained in RiseUp! during 2024.

In 2024 YW4A continued with the Rise Up! Leaderships trainings for young women. The training topics were contextualised to align with national relevant issues, and the young women were actively engaged in safe spaces established by the YW4A partners. A total of 2,129 young women were trained in Rise Up, resulting in a total of 4,302 young women being reached compared to the 4,200 country endline target. In Egypt, the World YWCA conducted Psychological First Aid (PFA) training, equipping selected Trainer of Trainers with the skills needed to provide essential emotional and psychological support to survivors of GBV and establish referral pathways to governmental and non-governmental agencies. Through this training, young women were empowered as key change agents in their communities and they gained a deep understanding of their role in assisting fellow young women. Additionally, the training emphasised the importance of self-care and emotional well-being. Apart from Rise Up! and other training opportunities, the consortium prioritised initiatives to build young women's leadership skills and confidence through mentorship and platforms to engage with high-level decision-makers. For instance, young leaders were actively involved in various high-level forums, not just as participants but also as panellists and moderators. In 2024, they played key roles in platforms such as Beijing +30, the Human Rights Council 56th session (HRC), and the Sexual Violence Research Initiative (SVRI), showcasing their leadership and advocacy on global stages.
Cohort 1 and 2 will cascade and train another cohort of 1,302 young women (cohort 3). During the course of 2023, the target was adjusted upwards to 1,700.

In Egypt, under Pathway 2, the Rise Up! training was conducted in safe spaces established in local partner organizations and through networking with secondary partners to implement the training in their venues. Participants represented a diverse range of marginalized groups, including refugees, people with disabilities, and survivors of gender-based violence. The content was tailored to address relevant issues facing young women in the Egyptian context, such as focusing on FGM as a prevalent harmful social norm in society. Additionally, topics were adjusted to accommodate the cultural and religious context of the community, with certain topics discarded for safety reasons, such as LGBTIQ topics.To complement the leadership skills acquired in the training, participants were engaged in advocacy activities and campaigns addressing issues related to GBV and women's political participation. Moreover, they participated in regional and international platforms such as Women Deliver 2023 and CSW 67, where they gained valuable knowledge and experience in advancing gender equality globally, engaging in fruitful discussions with other youth and activists.To address previous target shortfalls, the CL in Egypt increased the number of concurrent Rise Up! training groups in the 3rd quarter, particularly during the summer break when young women had more availability. As a result, the initial target for 2023, originally set at 1,302, was raised in October 2023 to 1,700. Surpassing expectations, Egypt achieved a total of 2,109 participants by the end of the year.

The target in 2022 was set to be 186 young women to be targeted by the Rise Up! Leadership training. This target was calculated based on that young women from cohort 1 would cascade the training to young women from cohort 2

Under Pathway 2, the YW4A programme enhances the leadership skills of young women through training and creating opportunities for them to train others and exercise their leadership, and be involved in advocacy. Throughout 2022, 64 young women were trained on the RiseUp! Leadership curriculum. Some of these young women have also participated in other trainings, for instance on legal and digital advocacy. The YW4A programme partners participated in various advocacy and dialogue spaces during the year, ensuring the involvement and active participation of young women and WROs.The partners in Egypt did not reach the targeted number of young women in 2022 due to the challenges faced by the programme during the first quarter of 2022 where two WROs opted out of the programme, which led to shifting the activities one quarter forward and this affected reaching the planned number of young women trained. The original strategy plan for engaging young women was modified to cover the shortage of 2022 during the first quarter of 2023 through duplicating the number of leadership sessions during the first quarter of 2023.
The total endline target of 4,200 young women being trained in Rise Up! has been achieved, therefore no targets are set for 2025.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.1 (WRG045,WRG047) IO1 Enhanced capacity of 16-28 WROs to amplify young women's voices

description.narrative: Under IO1 YW4A focuses on enhaning the organisational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organsations. The programme also envisages amplifying young women’s voices by promoting that WROs provide space in their internal organisations for young women and establish internal inclusive processes and practices in decision-making, management, and programming. And by working with WROs to include, represent, hear, mentor, support, and prepare young women to take part in advocacy initiatives, link them to strategic decision-making forums, and scale-up local advocacy strategies.

There were no changes in the composition of the WROs in Egypt during 2024. YW4A continued to build the capacity of the six WROs, through (refresher) digital and legal advocacy trainings, equipping young women and WROs with skills to engage policymakers effectively, and contributing to increased participation in legal and policy reforms for example on domestic violence, child marriage and SEAH policies. There was also strong emphasize on networking and coalition building, among other through participation in different regional coalitions, including the Hurra Coalition, to advocate for young women’s rights, policy and legal changes jointly with other organisations.
In 2022, YW4A is targeting the same 6 WROs as in 2021. Two new WROs are being identified as to replace the ones that dropped out in 2022.

Throughout 2022, YW4A partners undertook activities to build the WROs’ advocacy and organisational capacity. For example, through training on legal and digital advocacy the targeted WROs in Egypt have increased their capacity. Building on legal capacity strengthening undertaken in the first year, partners have enhanced capacity to scale up the critical work they have been doing in addressing women’s rights issues and using their experiences to call for action from duty bearers through various advocacy initiatives in line with the YW4A advocacy priorities and the laws and policies targeted under IO4. They now have the required skills to supplement their legal advocacy campaigns with media strategies. This increased capacity to engage in legal advocacy can also be seen in the way WROs and young women are being strategic when engaging national processes and different policy makers and actors in their country.In Egypt, the majority of the six organisations targeted by YW4A (similar to Y1) took part in these activities. In the first half of the year, two WROs left the programme. Potential candidates for replacement were identified and the process has led to two new WROs joining the programme as of 2023.
YW4A continues to work with the same WROs, including the two WROs that joined the programme in 2023 (replacing two organisations that dropped out during 2022).
